title: Lacson flags ‘double’ appropriations for flood projects in 2027 budget
summary: 'Some flood control projects received triple budget allocations. They were funded in 2024, 2025, and 2026 but were still under the proposed budget in 2027,' Lacson says

blocks.text: PING LACSON. Senator Ping Lacson at the briefing on the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of National Defense on October 19, 2026.
'Some flood control projects received triple budget allocations. They were funded in 2024, 2025, and 2026 but were still under the proposed budget in 2027,' Lacson says

items: Senator Panfilo Lacson has raised concerns about alleged double and triple appropriations for flood control projects in the proposed 2027 national budget, highlighting that some projects have already received funding in previous years.

Lacson also identified at least 30 alleged ghost multi-purpose buildings in the budget, questioning the legitimacy of funding for projects that have not been built despite receiving multiple allocations.

He criticized 'papogi spending' in the budget, which includes fragmented assistance programs, while stating he would scrutinize and seek the removal of questionable appropriations during the budget amendment process.

MANILA, Philippines – Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson has flagged alleged double and triple appropriations for some flood control projects in the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, saying some of them had already received funding in previous years.

“Not only double, but some flood control projects even received triple budget allocations. They were funded in 2024, 2025, and 2026 but were still under the proposed budget in 2027,” Lacson told reporters on Monday, November 23.

These projects are separate from at least 30 alleged ghost multi-purpose buildings (MPBs) that the senator said he had identified in the proposed Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) budget under the 2027 General Appropriations Bill (GAB).

Over the weekend, Lacson questioned the appropriations for 3,950 MPBs, apart from the 1,584 MPBs covered by the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) subprogram on financial assistance to local government units (LGUs) from 2022 to 2026.

Lacson said some of the MPBs appeared to be “ghost” projects. One infrastructure project, for instance, had received appropriations from 2024 to 2026, but no structure had been built at its designated site as of this year.

“Yes, we would move for its removal. That’s the logical thing to do,” Lacson said. “Why should we approve projects with massive allocations if they are not being established? Where are our public funds going?”

An initial investigation by Lacson’s office also found that the MPB projects involved alleged commissions of up to 10%. This is lower than the 15% to 30% kickbacks previously flagged in connection with anomalous flood control projects.

blocks.caption: House pushes thousands more multi-purpose buildings. Are they really needed?

blocks.text: Lacson said he would seek the removal of questionable infrastructure projects during the period of amendments to the budget bill.

“We continue to scrutinize the bill and find more of these kinds of appropriations. If there are double appropriations, one should be removed. If there are quadruple appropriations, three should be removed,” he added.

Lacson also criticized what he called “papogi spending” — spending meant to make one look good in the eyes of the public — in the proposed budget, including MPBs and P241 billion in what he described as “fragmented ayudas.”

Lacson questioned the continued funding of several government assistance programs, including the Medical Assistance for Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP), Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers (TUPAD), and Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS).
However, he said he would not “necessarily” seek the removal of these programs.
“They were fragmented ayuda programs. We already have 4Ps, UniFAST, and tertiary education law,” Lacson said. – Rappler.com
